740140101.text: Oh, what am I to do...

740140102.text: Huh? Are you okay? Sighing so sadly alone by the water like that... Did something bad happen?

740140103.text: Yes, and it wasn't any old "something bad," but something awful...

740140104.text: Ah! Apologies, I forgot to introduce myself. My name is Broglie, and I'm an entry-level researcher at the Fontaine Research Institute, and I was previously responsible for monitoring Fontaine's hydrology data.

740140106.text: *ahem* Simply put, it is all the data related to the various properties of water. For example, there's the temperature of various water layers, water level, rates of current flow and evaporation within set times, concentration of dissolved impurities...

740140108.text: Whoa, that all sounds really complicated!

740140109.text: It is, that's why people are needed — specifically, my colleagues and I — to collect this complex data and make observations so that we can detect changes in the water quality in advance.

740140110.text: If no one does this work, by the time we discover a huge problem, it will be too late to address it.

740140111.text: You know, that's one of the reasons those lovely Oceanids left Fontaine. There was a change in the water quality that made it unsuitable for them to live in—

740140114.text: Well... That's what I was told during my induction training, probably to rouse a semblance of personal responsibility in us. The point is, monitoring the hydrology data is pretty important work!

740140115.text: For instance, if a change in water quality nears the minimum coefficient, it could make the taste less smooth and refreshing...

740140117.text: Haha, well, that's what makes it the minimum coefficient, right? But if things got out of hand...

740140120.text: What, would the water turn into Fonta?

740140121.text: No, it would probably just lead to a mass extinction event all over Fontaine.

subQuests.subQuestName: Enter the sunken hydrology research station

740140201.text: #I'm counting on you to retrieve that data, kind {M#sir}{F#lady}!

740141201.speakerName: Conch Madeleine Stop Safe Operating Procedures
740141201.text: (This notebook must have been made of a water-resistant material — it's still in perfect condition even after all this time. There's also a sticky note on the cover.)

740141202.speakerName: Conch Madeleine Stop Safe Operating Procedures
740141202.text: "This is already the third time! Remember to follow the instructions precisely when operating! If we lose the data again, we won't get any more afternoon snacks for the month!"

740141204.speakerName: Conch Madeleine Stop Safe Operating Procedures
740141204.text: "...Standard Data Export Procedure: Confirm the energy storage device below the main console is online (in accordance with the Fontaine Research Institute Energy Conservation Regulation D-503, the device is turned off by default)..."

740141205.speakerName: Conch Madeleine Stop Safe Operating Procedures
740141205.text: "...When energy supply is normal, the green indicator on the main console will light up. At this time, pull the control lever on the left marked "DO NOT TOUCH OR ELSE" to print out the observation data..."

740141206.speakerName: Conch Madeleine Stop Safe Operating Procedures
740141206.text: "...Data should be printed at least once every 3 months, or else some data may be lost..."

740140801.text: Great! Now we can turn the console on!

740140802.text: What does the instruction manual say... Okay, next, we just need to pull that lever that says "Do NOT touch under any circumstances!" on it, and we can export the recorded data...

740140804.text: That's what the manual says. Paimon guesses to prevent other people from misusing it? Weird...

740140806.text: You pull the lever down.\nAfter some rumbling and shaking, the machine spits out a stack of paper tape...

740140807.text: This should be the monitoring data Broglie needs...

740140808.text: Paimon can't understand any of it, but all we need is to bring it back to him and we're good, right?

740140902.text: What does the instruction manual say... Okay, next we just need to pull that lever that says "Do NOT touch under any circumstances!" on it, and we can export the recorded data...

740140906.text: You pull the lever down.\nAfter some rumbling and shaking, the machine spits out a stack of paper tape...

740140907.text: Hmm... Paimon doesn't have a clue what's on it, but it looks pretty important...

740140908.text: #{NICKNAME}, why don't we keep this paper tape for now? Who knows, it might come in handy later...

740141101.text: Yes, that's it, that's it! All the data from this station's been recovered now!

740141102.text: Well, that's good... Wait a minute, did you say "this station"?

740141103.text: Yes! We have three observation stations and one central processing station in total, each with their own independent datasets.

740141104.text: So, in order to convey the need for monitoring to my supervisor, the data from the remaining two stations still needs to be recovered and then analyzed at the central processing station...

740141105.text: Uh, alright, Paimon will bite — do you also need us to salvage the other two stations?

740141106.text: Oh, of course not! The other two observation stations were spared from the lab disaster and continue to stand proudly on solid ground!

740141108.text: It's just that... those two stations have been taken over by some fellows from Snezhnaya...

740141109.text: From Snezhnaya... Hang on, you're not talking about the Fatui, are you?

740141110.text: That's them! They claimed that they got permission from the Maison Gestion to take over the stations. They won't let us anywhere near them, let alone retrieve the data.

740141111.text: As for the Maison Gestion... As you may know, verifying anything with the Maison Gestion is harder than trying to catch lightning in a bottle.

740141113.text: Yeah, since it's the Fatui we're talking about, they might actually be planning to use the observation stations to do something bad...

740141114.text: #Paimon doesn't super want to help, but... *sigh* {NICKNAME}, we should take a look just in case...

740141115.text: #Thank you so much, kind {M#sir}{F#lady}! I'll mark the locations of the Pate de Fruit Station and Crepes Suzette Station on your map now!

740141117.text: Yes! And they do sound sweet and tasty, don't they? Just the way life ought to be!

740141118.text: By the way, this place is the Conch Madeleine Station. Imagine, if you would, breaking off a small piece of Conch Madeleine, steeping it in warm water or Tisane, and drinking it all up...

740141119.text: That's what our tea times were like before. *sigh* I never thought the station would end up sinking like this...

740141120.text: Anyway, for me to be happy and free again... I mean, for scientific advancement and the future of humanity, I'm counting on you to help me recover that old monitoring data!

740140601.text: This looks like the central control room Broglie was talking about, right?

740141701.text: Huh? Wait a minute, now that Paimon's looking at these locations, it seems like we've already been to them before...

740141703.text: We've already sent those Fatui running for the hills.

740141704.text: And, we already have that data you're looking for...

740141705.text: You show Broglie the paper tapes you got earlier...

740141706.text: Ahhhh! Yes, this is it, this is it! You two are angels, angels sent from the heavens to save me from my misery and return me to my happy life of ease—

740141707.text: Hey! What about all that science stuff?
